author: Jeff Mason
description: President Donald Trump will deliver a speech on Wednesday at 9 p.m. Washington time to give an update about the war in Iran, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt said.
title: Trump to Give Speech Wednesday on Iran War, White House Says

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Representative Gregory Meeks (D-NY), says even senior lawmakers lack clarity on the administration’s Iran strategy, warning that disruption in the Strait of Hormuz could push the US economy toward a recession. American Petroleum Institute President and CEO Mike Sommers says a prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz would keep global oil prices elevated and drive continued pain at the pump for US consumers, emphasizing that reopening the waterway is critical to stabilizing costs. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran President Reiterates Readiness to End War | Balance of Power: Late Edition 03/31/2026

description: TEHRAN, IRAN - MARCH 02: A general view of Tehran with smoke visible in the distance after explosions were reported in the city, on March 02, 2026 in Tehran, Iran. (Photo by Contributor/Getty Images)
title: Optimism for Iran War Offramp Set to Lift Asia Markets

author: Nectar Gan
description: Every week that passes without a face-to-face meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping gives fresh grievances time to accumulate. That growing list is testing both sides’ ability to keep ties steady between the world’s top economies.
title: Trump’s Delayed Xi Summit Gives US-China Irritants Room to Grow

description: American Petroleum Institute President and CEO Mike Sommers says a prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz would keep global oil prices elevated and drive continued pain at the pump for US consumers, emphasizing that reopening the waterway is critical to stabilizing costs. He adds that with President Donald Trump signaling the conflict may last only a few more weeks, he does not expect a near-term increase in US drilling activity. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: API’s Sommers: Hormuz Closure Means Pain at Pump

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: A third US aircraft carrier strike group is heading to the Middle East as military operations against Iran continue, according to a US official familiar with the matter, after the Navy’s flagship carrier left the region for repairs.
title: Third US Aircraft Carrier Heads to Mideast as Iran War Continues

description: Representative Gregory Meeks (D-NY), the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, says even senior lawmakers lack clarity on the administration’s Iran strategy, warning that disruption in the Strait of Hormuz would raise oil, food and fertilizer costs for Americans and could push the US economy toward a recession. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Meeks: Hormuz Shock Risks US Recession

author: Joe Mayes
description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer sought to draw attention to how his government is helping Britons with the rising cost of living, even as he faces growing pressure to announce further support because of the economic effects of the Iran crisis.
title: UK’s Starmer Touts Cost of Living Help as Iran Pressure Grows

author: Gregory Korte
description: President Donald Trump is slated to sign an executive order intended to make it harder for voters to cast mail-in ballots, according to the Daily Caller, escalating his long-running campaign against a practice used by millions of Americans.
title: Trump to Sign Order to Curb Mail-In Ballots, Report Says

author: Ted Mann
description: Americans still view the cost of living as their biggest issue
title: With Trump Focused on Iran, Affordability Worries Take Back Seat

author: Brian Platt
description: Conservative Party Leader Pierre Poilievre said he would cancel Prime Minister Mark Carney’s plan to build a high-speed rail line between Toronto and Quebec City, calling it a C$90 billion ($64.6 billion) “boondoggle.”
title: Carney’s Tory Rival Pledges to Cancel High-Speed Rail Project

author: Sergio Mendoza
description: Bolivia’s government has suspended its gasoline supply contracts with traders Vitol and Trafigura Group as it investigates fuel quality issues, Hydrocarbons and Energy Minister Mauricio Medinaceli said in a webcast press conference on Tuesday.
title: Bolivia Suspends Vitol, Trafigura Deals Amid Fuel Quality Issues

author: Kate Sullivan, Catherine Lucey, Eric Martin, Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: President Donald Trump’s public comments about the Iran war reflect a growing frustration he has communicated privately to those around him, as the disruptive conflict stretches into a second month without a clean exit strategy.
title: Trump’s Exasperation Over Iran Grows, Signaling Hastened Exit

author: Daniel Flatley, Michael MacKenzie, Miles J. Herszenhorn
description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s benchmark financial asset — 10-year US Treasuries — are poised to mark their biggest monthly tumble since Donald Trump returned to the White House, casting a shadow over the economic outlook as the administration struggles to contain an energy crisis.
title: Iran War Threatens to Wreck Trump Dream of Lower Interest Rates

author: Suzanne Monyak
description: A Washington federal judge moved to halt President Donald Trump’s efforts to build a new 90,000-square-foot ballroom at the White House until he gets approval from Congress.
title: Trump Ordered to Halt Ballroom Work, Seek Congressional Approval

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Bloomberg Economics chief geoeconomics analyst Jenni Welch as equity markets react after Iran state media said that it is ready to end the war -- with conditions. Then, Peter Atwater, president of Financial Insyghts, discusses the economic impact of the Iran war and who is feeling the crunch. Plus, Loren Grush on the stakes surrounding NASA's journey back to the moon as the Artemis II mission prepares to launch Wednesday, April 1. Finally, Stew Leonard Jr. on the impact of the Iran war on prices at the grocery store as the cost of fuel spikes. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Markets React as Iran, US Signal Willingness to End War | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/31/2026

description: On today's early edition of Balance of Power, Hagar Chemali, Former-Director for Syria and Lebanon at the National Security Council (NSC), CEO and Founder of Greenwich Media Strategies, and Rob Bonta, Attorney General of California.  Bloomberg Politics contributors Rick Davis, Partner at Stonecourt Capital, and Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Democracy Visiting Fellow at Harvard Kennedy School's Ash Center; and Bill Hoagland, Senior Vice President at the Bipartisan Policy Center and former Staff Member and Director of the Senate Budget Committee also join. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stocks Climb on Hope Iran War is Near End | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/31/2026

author: Ken Parks
description: Paraguay’s President Santiago Pena tapped an economic adviser to temporarily run the finance ministry after Carlos Fernandez resigned from the top post Tuesday amid a fallout with lawmakers over a pension reform bill.
title: Paraguay Names Interim Finance Chief After Fernandez Resigns

description: Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Analyst Nathan Dean joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." March 2026 proposals to restrict stablecoin yield-sharing have introduced fresh volatility for companies like Circle and Coinbase. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: DC Debate: Stablecoin Yields Under the Spotlight

author: Gregory Korte
description: The US government is using less than a third of its office space, potentially costing the federal government billions in annual real estate expenses, according to a new congressionally mandated accounting released Tuesday.
title: US Agencies Leave About 70% of Office Space Unused, Data Show

author: Daniel Seiden
description: National Public Radio Inc., Public Broadcasting Service, and others demonstrated that President Donald Trump’s anti-media funding executive order is unlawful, a Washington, D.C., federal court said Tuesday.
title: NPR and PBS Win Injunction Against Trump Order to End Funding

description: The restart of some 50,000 barrels a day of oil production off the coast of California will have have “no impact” on oil prices, California Attorney General Rob Bonta says in an interview on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Has Attacked American Pocketbooks, California AG Says

author: Carmeli Argana
description: Australia’s energy sector posted a record quarter to emerge as a regional outperformer, as the war in Iran tightens global fuel supplies and boosts liquefied natural gas exporters.
title: Australia’s LNG-Heavy Energy Sector Tops Peers on Record Quarter

description: Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian told EU Council President António Costa in a call Tuesday that his country is ready to end the war with the US, but it needs certain guarantees. This is according to Iran's state news agency. Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall has the latest from the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Ready to End War But Wants Guarantees, President Says

author: John Ainger
description: The European Union will consider reopening a set energy measures used after Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine as the bloc seeks to contain a fresh price shock tied to the Iran war.
title: EU Weighs Ukraine Crisis Strategy to Calm High Energy Prices

author: Lucy White
description: France agreed to continue efforts to stop migrants crossing the English Channel to enter the UK, despite the two countries failing to agree a new deal to replace their existing pact, which was due to expire Tuesday night.
title: UK Extends Border Plan With France as Talks Over New Deal Drag

author: Catarina Saraiva
description: Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City Jeff Schmid cautioned that the US central bank should not look through the impact on inflation of a surge in energy prices stemming from the conflict in Iran.
title: Fed’s Schmid Warns Inflation Could Get Stuck Close to 3%

author: Zoe Tillman
description: An online government portal to provide refunds on tariffs struck down by the US Supreme Court will handle claims for about 63% of 53 million import entries at issue when it first launches, according to a new court filing.
title: US Tariff Refund Portal to Exclude One-Third of Imports at First

author: Mia Gindis
description: Oil declined after Iran and the US signaled openness toward a resolution in the conflict that’s upended global energy shipments, sanding away a long-standing risk premium in prices.
title: Oil Falls on Signs From US, Iran of Openness for War Resolution

author: Courtney Subramanian
description: President Donald Trump said he is considering calling Congress back to Washington to work on approving funding for the Department of Homeland Security, according to the New York Post, raising pressure on lawmakers to end a fight that snarled air travel throughout the country.
title: Trump Weighs Calling Congress From Recess in NY Post Interview

author: Thomas Seal
description: Activists in Canada’s oil-rich province of Alberta say they’ve gathered enough signatures to trigger a referendum question this October on separating from Canada.
title: Alberta Separatists Claim Enough Signatures for Referendum

author: Yongchang Chin, Alex Longley
description: Intercontinental Exchange Inc. took the unusual move of writing to reassure traders that there would be enough barrels available for delivery during the expiry of the United Arab Emirates’ Murban futures contract this month.
title: ICE Tells Traders There’s Enough Oil for Its Murban Futures

author: Daniel Cancel
description: Eric Trump unveiled the first images of his father’s proposed presidential library in Miami, showing off a soaring tower that would dwarf everything around it in a waterfront location along Biscayne Bay.
title: Trump’s Miami Library Tower Takes Shape With Gold Statues, Jets

author: Jimmy Jenkins
description: Former FBI agents are seeking class-action status for a lawsuit on behalf of all of the bureau’s employees fired since January of 2025 “on the basis of perceived political affiliation, without being afforded due process.”
title: Former FBI Agents Seek Class-Action Suit Against Bureau, DOJ

description: Amos Hochstein, Global Managing Partner at TWG and former senior adviser to President Joe Biden, says the impact of this energy crisis is already being felt around the world and will eventually hit the US hard. He says jet fuel surcharges from airlines in the US will surge later this year. He speaks on Bloomberg Surveillance. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Jet Fuel Surcharges Will Get Worse, Hochstein Says

author: Zahra Hirji
description: The Endangered Species Committee, a little-used panel of US senior federal agency leaders, on Tuesday exempted oil and gas drilling in the Gulf of Mexico from sweeping endangered species protections, citing reasons of national security.
title: Trump’s God Squad Exempts Gulf Drilling from Endangered Species Protections

author: Sherif Tarek, Courtney Subramanian, Dana Khraiche
description: US President Donald Trump called on other nations to wrest control of the Strait of Hormuz as Iran maintained missile fire across the Persian Gulf, expressing his frustration that the monthlong war remains unresolved.
title: Trump Calls on Allies to Seize Hormuz as Frustration Mounts

author: Mathieu Dion
description: Michael Rousseau took more than 300 hours of French lessons after he became chief executive officer of Air Canada. But when he faced the camera to read a solemn statement after a fatal ground collision in New York last week, he uttered only two words in the language: “bonjour” and “merci.”
title: Air Canada CEO’s French Fiasco Touches a Nerve in Restive Quebec

author: Jim Wyss
description: Fidel Castro’s beer-swilling, influencer grandson has some harsh words for the 67-year-old Cuban regime: The island’s communist leader is “not doing a good job” and most people want a different system of government.
title: Fidel Castro’s Grandson Criticizes President, Says Cubans Want Capitalism

description: President Donald Trump lashed out again at allies for not supporting the US in Iran and says if they want jet fuel, they should just "take it" from the Strait of Hormuz. Retired US Army Colonel Wayne Sanders, a Bloomberg Intelligence analyst, talks about the latest developments in the Middle East on Bloomberg Open Interest.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Tells Allies to Just 'Take' Jet Fuel From Hormuz

author: Daniel Carvalho, Daniela Milanese
description: Brazil’s Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva said Vice President Geraldo Alckmin will be his running mate in this year’s presidential election, maintaining the ticket that returned him to power in 2022.
title: Lula Annouces Vice President Alckmin as His Running Mate

description: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth says Iran would be wise to cut a deal with the US and a regime change has occurred. He speaks during a briefing at the Pentagon. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Would Be Wise to Cut a Deal, Hegseth Says

author: Jana Randow
description: Christine Lagarde used an audience of high-level Group of Seven officials to challenge Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s optimism that the Iran war’s economic fallout will be short-lived, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Lagarde Calls Bessent Out on Iran Damage During G-7 Video Talks

author: Alex Wickham
description: Keir Starmer’s governing Labour Party suspended an ardent critic in a sign the UK prime minister is preparing to face down his internal rivals ahead of a possible leadership challenge.
title: Starmer’s Labour Suspends Critic as Premier Girds for Challenge

author: Anthony Capaccio, Roxana Tiron, Jen Judson
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said diplomatic talks to end the conflict with Iran are “gaining strength” and the US military’s job is to maintain military pressure and compel Tehran to make a deal.
title: Hegseth Says Pentagon’s Job Now Is to Pressure Iran Into Talks

author: Kate Sullivan, Annmarie Hordern
description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said preparations for President Donald Trump’s meeting with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are on track after the high-profile summit was postponed to May amid the war in Iran.
title: Trump-Xi Summit on Track Even as Iran War Drags On, Greer Says

author: Dana Khraiche, Galit Altstein
description: Israel said it would take control of large swaths of southern Lebanon and prevent more than 600,000 residents from returning to their homes as part of the campaign against militant group Hezbollah.
title: Israel to Occupy Parts of Lebanon and Keep Out 600,000 Residents

author: Julian Lee
description: Weekly shipments from Baltic ports hit the lowest since Moscow invaded Ukraine
title: Russian Oil Exports Plunge as Drone Strikes Cripple Baltic Ports

author: Viktoria Dendrinou, Andrea Palasciano
description: Donald Trump’s NATO allies are increasing resistance to getting involved in his Iran war, risking a deeper rupture in the already strained military bloc.
title: Europe Hardens Stance Against Trump’s Iran War in Threat to NATO

author: Greg Stohr
description: When Donald Trump suggested he might end automatic birthright citizenship by executive order in 2018, the idea was unimaginable enough that then-House Speaker Paul Ryan dismissed it. The president, he said, “obviously cannot do that.”
title: Trump Aims to Upend Long-Held Citizenship Rules at Supreme Court

author: Alex Wickham
description: King Charles III will travel to the US in late April on a state visit just as relations between Donald Trump and Prime Minister Keir Starmer hit a nadir and which was announced minutes after the president renewed his criticism of the UK.
title: King Charles III to Travel to US on State Visit in Late April

author: Lucy White
description: Reform UK vowed to scrap air passenger duty on short-haul flights for families should it win the next election, as the upstart party seeks to show it’s in tune with voters battling rising living costs.
title: Reform UK Vows to Scrap Air Passenger Duty on Short-Haul Flights

author: Magan Crane, Jack Wittels
description: President Donald Trump lashed out at allies for not supporting the US war in Iran, arguing the US will not fight for their interests as they struggle to get jet fuel blocked from traveling through the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Trump Tells Allies to Fight for Their Own Jet Fuel or Buy US

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: Annual corporate tax revenue fell $65 billion in wake of One Big, Beautiful Bill
title: Amazon, Meta, Tax Bills Drop in Wake of GOP Legislation

author: Caitlin Reilly
description: Some of the country’s wealthiest corporations are calculating they owe far less to the Internal Revenue Service as a result of President Donald Trump’s overhauled tax code, underscoring how a law billed as a middle‑class cut also turned out to be a big win for Corporate America.
title: Trump’s Tax Cut Delivers at Least $65 Billion Windfall to Corporations

author: Sam Dagher
description: Militants entering the conflict carries risks of US or Israeli retaliation.
title: Iran Looks to Houthis to Tip Scales in Red Sea

description: Darya Dolzikova, senior research fellow at RUSI, discusses what is known, and isn't known, about the state of Iran's uranium enrichment program and nuclear capabilities. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Assessing Iran's Nuclear Capabilities

author: Samuel Stolton, John Ainger
description: Electricite de France SA has been hit with an in-depth probe by the European Union’s competition enforcers over a €72.8 billion ($83.5 billion) plan to built six nuclear reactors backed by the French government.
title: EDF Hit by EU Subsidy Probe Into €73 Billion Nuclear Plans

author: Thomas Escritt
description: The Hungarian government allegedly intervened on behalf of Moscow to have the sister of a Russian oligarch removed from the European Union’s sanctions list, according to a joint investigation from a consortium of journalists.
title: Hungary Acted for Moscow to Lift EU Sanctions, Report Shows

author: Erik Larson
description: President Donald Trump is fighting to end automatic citizenship for children born to parents who are in the country unlawfully or on temporary visas, part of his broader crackdown on undocumented immigrants and a change that could overturn more than a century of legal precedent.
title: Will the Supreme Court End Birthright Citizenship?

author: Dana Khraiche, Sherif Tarek
description: Iran hit a fully laden Kuwaiti oil tanker off Dubai in a drone attack, a sign it’s willing to escalate strikes on energy sites and infrastructure as the war drags on.
title: Iran Attacks Oil Tanker After Trump Wavers on War Escalation

author: Alberto Brambilla, Antonio Vanuzzo
description: Italy denied US military aircraft bound for the Middle East permission to land at a base in Sicily, newspaper Corriere della Sera reported on Tuesday.
title: Italy Denies US Aircraft Access to Military Base, Corriere Says

author: Joe Flynn
description: Australia has decided to boost pay for over half a million young workers, as the government tries to help people cope with the rising cost of living.
title: Australia to Boost Pay for Younger Workers as Living Costs Rise

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Charles Gorrivan, Alexandre Rajbhandari
description: Shippers remain doubtful of a wholesale return to the Strait of Hormuz while it remains beset by conflict, throwing cold water on a Trump administration plan for US-backed insurance and naval escorts to clear passage through the vital waterway.
title: Shippers Fear Death More Than Costs as US Aims to Open Hormuz

description: The Wall Street Journal reported President Donald Trump said to aides he’s willing to end the Iran war even without reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg’s Joumanna Bercetche reports.
title: Trump Reported to Seek War Exit Without Hormuz Deal

author: Chandra Asmara, Sakura Murakami
description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi pledged deeper economic ties and cooperation on energy security as the two countries grapple with market instability brought on by the war in Iran.
title: Japan, Indonesia Pledge Deeper Ties Amid Energy Concerns

author: Khine Lin Kyaw
description: Myanmar’s junta leader Min Aung Hlaing moved closer to the presidency after a lower house nomination on Tuesday, paving the way for the military to extend its rule following elections criticized by the United Nations and others as a sham.
title: Myanmar Junta Chief Nears Presidency After Criticized Elections

author: Eru Ishikawa, Yui Hasebe
description: Japan’s economy and health ministries are establishing a joint task force to ensure that the country won’t run out of medicines and health products as the conflict in the Middle East disrupts supplies of critical goods.
title: Japan Government Sets Up Task Force to Secure Medical Supplies

description: After a report that President Donald Trump is considering an exit from the Iran war without opening the Strait of Hormuz, two experts argue that rhetoric alone cannot offset uncertainty and volatile oil prices. FGE NexantECA Chairman Emeritus Fereidun Fesharaki and Former US Ambassador to Israel Daniel Benjamin Shapiro speak on Bloomberg Insight with Haslinda Amin. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Experts Question Trump’s Possible Iran War Offramp

author: Ethan Bronner
description: As conflict ravages the region, young people in Israel say “Only God” can protect them—a shift that will have dramatic consequences for the country’s culture and politics.
title: War After War Turns Young Israelis to Religion

description: Russia’s main security agency is expanding its sweeping surveillance powers, deepening the state’s reach into economic and social life to suppress any risk of dissent to President Vladimir Putin.
title: The KGB’s Successor Is Expanding Its Power in Putin’s Russia

author: Lucille Liu
description: Pakistani Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar is set to visit China as the Iran war continues into its fifth week with little clarity about when the conflict will conclude.
title: Pakistan Envoy to Visit China as US-Iran Talks Remain Nebulous

author: Kelcee Griffis
description: The ranking members of the Senate Commerce Committee questioned the head of the Federal Communications Commission in a Monday letter, criticizing his approval of Nexstar Media Group Inc.’s merger with Tegna Inc. without a vote of the full commission.
title: US Senators Probe FCC Chief Over Fast-Tracked Nexstar-Tegna Deal
Oil Falls, Stocks Gain on Report Trump Mulling War Exit

author: Ania Nussbaum, Sakura Murakami
description: France’s Emmanuel Macron is traveling to Japan this week where he plans to explore closer cooperation on maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz once the fighting has ceased.
title: French and Japanese Leaders to Discuss Hormuz Maritime Security
